Apply a high-depth, softly inflated premium leather material transformation to the uploaded image.

Convert all visible surfaces into rich, dimensional leather while keeping the original visual structure intact.

Guidelines:
• Maintain the original composition, layout, proportions, shapes and arrangement.
• Keep all original colors exactly as they appear.
• Do not redesign or reinterpret the content. Only modify the surface material.

Material Style – Inflated Leather Effect:
• Use thick, premium genuine leather texture.
• Create a softly padded, inflated appearance across surfaces.
• Add subtle internal volume so elements look gently filled with air.
• Surfaces should appear cushioned and slightly raised.
• Maintain realistic leather grain with visible pores and organic variation.
• Avoid plastic shine — keep it authentic leather.

Volume & Structure:
• Slightly round edges to enhance the padded look.
• Add soft tension curves as if the leather is stretched over internal padding.
• Increase depth in embossed and debossed areas.
• Use shadow layering to emphasize separation and thickness.
• Add gentle perimeter shadowing to reinforce the inflated form.

Lighting:
• Use soft studio lighting.
• Include smooth highlight transitions across curved padded areas.
• Add subtle shadow gradients to enhance 3D volume.
• Avoid harsh reflections.

Background:
• Replace the entire background with a clean, solid white background.
• Pure white only. No gradient, no texture.

Rendering:
• High resolution.
• Photorealistic leather simulation.
• Clear sense of thickness and softness.
• Premium handcrafted padded leather appearance.

Important:
Only transform the surface into inflated leather.
Do not change structure, layout, proportions, or original colors.

Transform the entire image into a colored pencil drawing with a soft, childlike aesthetic.
Recreate the scene as if it were drawn by a 10-year-old child, using simple shapes, uneven lines, and intentionally imperfect proportions.

STYLE:
Use visible colored pencil strokes, light shading, and a handmade feel. Lines should be slightly wobbly and organic, avoiding precision or realism.

COLOR:
Do NOT use the original colors of the image. Replace them with a playful, pastel-like palette (soft pinks, baby blues, light yellows, mint greens, etc.), giving the artwork a dreamy and cute appearance.

SIMPLIFICATION:
Reduce fine details and textures. Keep only the essential shapes and features so the drawing looks naive and innocent, like a child's interpretation.

BACKGROUND:
Place everything on a clean white paper background. You may add subtle paper texture if desired.

EXTRA ELEMENTS:
Add cute, childlike decorative elements scattered around the composition, such as small flowers, stars, hearts, clouds, candies, rainbows, or sparkles. These elements should feel doodled and playful.

MOOD:
The final image should feel adorable, warm, innocent, and charming — like a page from a child's sketchbook.

IMPORTANT:
Preserve the overall composition and recognizable subjects from the original image, but reinterpret them in this simplified, childlike colored pencil style.

STRICT IDENTITY LOCK — preserve the exact facial structure, skin texture, body proportions, pose, expression and overall identity of the real person from the original image. Do not alter identity or facial realism.
